images.title: Diagonals bisecting at 90° make a rhombus
images.purpose: Shows quadrilateral ABCD whose diagonals bisect each other at right angles at O, so the four triangles are congruent and all four sides are equal.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. One large quadrilateral standing on a corner in the centre, its unequal diagonals crossing at a right angle.
images.exact_structure: One quadrilateral ABCD in dark outline: A on the left, B at the top, C on the right, D at the bottom. The horizontal diagonal AC is longer than the vertical diagonal BD; they cross at O with a small filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) square right angle mark. Half diagonals OA and OC each carry one short tick mark; half diagonals OB and OD each carry two short tick marks. Triangle AOB is lightly filled teal (#0072B2) and triangle COB is lightly filled amber (#E69F00). All four sides AB, BC, CD and DA carry three short tick marks each, showing they are equal. The letters A, B, C, D sit outside their corners and O below and right of the crossing. Nothing else in the frame.

images.takeaway: If the diagonals bisect each other at right angles, the quadrilateral is a rhombus.

images.context: SAS on ∆AOB and ∆COB (OA = OC, right angles, OB common), and likewise round the figure.

image_decisions.why: The two shaded congruent triangles at the crossing show why all four sides must be equal.
